'''Pedro Gil Ferreira''' (born 18 March 1968) is a Portuguese [[astrophysicist]] and author.<ref name="Levin2016">{{cite book|author=Janna Levin|title=Black Hole Blues and Other Songs from Outer Space|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=AzHjCgAAQBAJ&pg=PA226|date=29 March 2016|publisher=Knopf Doubleday Publishing Group|isbn=978-0-307-95820-4|pages=226–}}</ref><ref name="Halpern2012">{{cite book|author=Paul Halpern|title=Edge of the Universe: A Voyage to the Cosmic Horizon and Beyond|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=P8nkJdkApOUC&pg=PT57|date=10 August 2012|publisher=[[John Wiley & Sons]]|isbn=978-1-118-23460-0|pages=57–}}</ref> As of 2016 he is Professor of Astrophysics at the [[University of Oxford]],<ref name=sample>[https://www.theguardian.com/science/2016/feb/09/watch-this-spacetime-gravitational-wave-discovery-expected "Watch this spacetime: gravitational wave discovery expected"]. ''[[The Guardian]]'',  Ian Sample, 9 February 2016</ref> and a fellow of [[Wolfson College, Oxford|Wolfson College]].

==Education and early life==
Ferreira was born in Lisbon, Portugal, and attended the [[Technical University of Lisbon]], where he studied engineering from 1986 to 1991. While there, he taught himself [[general relativity]]. He studied for a PhD in theoretical physics at [[Imperial College London]], supervised by [[Andreas Albrecht (cosmologist)|Andy Albrecht]].{{citation needed|date=January 2018}}{{when|date=January 2018}}

==Research and career==
He occupied postdoctoral positions at [[University of California Berkeley|Berkeley]] and [[CERN]], before returning to the UK to join the faculty in the astrophysics department at the [[University of Oxford]] as a research fellow and lecturer.<ref>{{cite book|title=Symmetry: Dimensions of Particle Physics|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=UdTyAAAAMAAJ|year=2007|publisher=Fermi National Accelerator Lab.|page=92}}</ref> He became Professor of Astrophysics there in 2008. He has been director of the Programme on Computational Cosmology at the [[Oxford Martin School]] since 2010, and also runs an astrophysics 'artist in residency' programme. Ferreira regularly lectures at the [[African Institute for Mathematical Sciences]], and has frequently appeared on TV and radio as a science commentator.

Ferreira's main interests are in general relativity and theoretical cosmology. He has authored more than 100 publications in peer-reviewed scientific journals.<ref>[https://scholar.google.ca/citations?user=xzt4czQAAAAJ&hl=en Google Scholar report for Pedro Ferreira]</ref> With Michael Joyce, in 1997, he was one of the first to propose [[Quintessence (physics)|quintessence]] [[scalar field]] models as a possible explanation of [[dark energy]]. Ferreira was also a member of the [[Millimeter Anisotropy eXperiment IMaging Array|MAXIMA]] and [[BOOMERanG experiment|BOOMERanG]] balloon-borne CMB experiments, which measured the [[Baryon acoustic oscillations|acoustic peaks]] of the CMB. He is currently involved in several proposals to test general relativity using the [[Euclid (spacecraft)|Euclid spacecraft]] and [[Square Kilometre Array]] radio telescope.

===Media===
Ferreira is a regular contributor to the scientific press, including ''[[Nature (journal)|Nature]]'', ''[[Science (journal)|Science]]'', and ''[[New Scientist]]'', and has authored two popular science books on cosmology and the history of [[general relativity]]. One of them, ''The Perfect Theory'', was shortlisted for the 2014 [[Royal Society Prizes for Science Books|Royal Society Winton Prize for Science Books]]. He regularly appears on TV and radio to discuss astrophysics and cosmology news stories, and has contributed to several science and mathematics documentaries for the [[BBC]], [[Discovery Channel]], and others.  In 2016, he served on the editorial board of the '' Open Journal of Astrophysics''.<ref>[http://www.nature.com/news/open-journals-that-piggyback-on-arxiv-gather-momentum-1.19102 "Open journals that piggyback on arXiv gather momentum"]. ''Nature'', Volume 530, Issue 7588, Toolbox Elizabeth Gibney, 4 January 2016</ref>
